title: Label-only output limits score information but does not eliminate leakage

invariants.description: Label-only output must reduce correct reconstructions significantly on the same targets (observed 200 → 168 of 200, McNemar p = 2.3e-10; 20-seed max 1.5e-5).
At least 30% of targets must become ambiguous without a score (observed 104/200 = 52.0%).

A NEW attack against label-only output must still beat the auxiliary-only attacker by ≥ 10 points (observed +30/200 = +15.0%; 20-seed range +14.0 to +23.5 points): records near the decision boundary still leak.
Leakage under label-only output must remain significant (observed p = 9.3e-10; 20-seed max 3.7e-9).

rationale: Removing the score removes most of the signal, but whenever the private attribute flips the decision the label alone reveals it. Label-only output is a mitigation, not a guarantee.
